Based on the consistent and overwhelming epidemiological data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), men who have sex with men (categorized in the options as homosexual males) account for the vast majority of new HIV diagnoses and overall infections within the Latino/Hispanic population in the United States. This trend mirrors the broader national epidemiology, where sexual transmission among men who have sex with men remains the single largest transmission category, far exceeding the proportions seen in heterosexual males, females, or injection drug users.
